newsitem.title: GABON: Ruling party wins Gabon parliamentary poll.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party wins Gabon parliamentary poll.

text.p: President Omar Bongo's ruling party has won a comfortable majority in Gabon's new parliament following Sunday's election runoffs, partial provisional results showed on Tuesday.
With the results of 30 of the national assembly's 120 seats to come, the opposition had mustered only a handful of seats.
Election officials said results from local polling stations showed Bongo's Democratic Party had so far won 22 seats on Sunday, taking its tally to 68. Two smaller allied parties won two seats each.
The main opposition National Woodcutters Rally (RNB), who won control of Libreville in chaotic October municipal elections, still had only three seats, which it won in the December 15 first round.
The elections are part of a democratic timetable brokered in Paris in 1994 after political violence shook the oil-producing Central African nation, killing over a dozen people.
The National Electoral Commission must check the results, which will be formally announced by the Interior Ministry and proclaimed by the Constitutional Court.
Sunday's poll was marred by scattered incidents. Two people were wounded in the northern town of Bitam in a shooting.
Rivalry among Bongo's own supporters has been intense. Many stood as independents after failing to win the party ticket.
The elections are Gabon's second multiparty legislative polls. The first were in 1990 when a wave of democratic reform swept across Africa after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba. His presidential term ends in 1998.
